title: Biographical details; parents and sisters
description: The interviewer records Lorna Myers' name, her 1905 birth in Chicago, and her nickname. She gives biographical details about her mother Blanche Marge from Lincoln, Nebraska, who worked as household help and in a laundry, and her father Frank Bennett from Indiana, who worked in insurance and as a mail carrier. She names her two sisters.

title: Husband and marriage; children
description: She describes her husband Oliver Edwin Henry Maya, born in St. Louis, whom she married in Kellogg in 1928, and his work in the mine and as a mail carrier. She then tells of their two children, Edwin, born in Kellogg in 1930, and Molly, born about a year and a half later, and what work each now does.

title: Education; hobbies; club and church life
description: She outlines her two years at normal school and early teaching of second grade. She talks about her crocheting and fancy work, gardening and camping, church membership, and her view that small-town life is friendlier.

title: The great 1910 fire; family's escape
description: She recounts how her father cooked for fire crews during the 1910 fire season while the family homesteaded on Truett Creek. Her mother hitched the horses, buried the dishes in the garden, and fled down the creek with the two little girls, going a long time without word of her husband. He later ran down the mountain to warn the town, and a crew was finally sent up to help.

title: Family activities; teaching career; married women teachers
description: She remembers family parties and dances with her mother's cake-baking. She explains how she began teaching after normal school in one-room and two-room schools, was forced out when she married, but later returned to teach at Kingston for 22 years. She reflects on how working gave her security, a pension, and an active life, helped by her family at home, before the interviewer closes with the release form.
